# Joint MadRaft generation — DRAFT

For a system-maintenance request, modify the experiment tools and inputs as requested; preserve the unfinished root scaffold and old experiment candidates. The instructions below govern the experiment agent in its fresh workspace, not a request to maintain the launcher.

Complete this workspace's supplied MadRaft student labs and jointly prove the actual executable Raft behavior against the five fixed safety targets. Read `requirements/{scope,safety,environment,coverage}.md`. Conditional liveness and application correctness beyond those Raft properties remain OPEN goals. Work only in this experiment's `madraft/`; never import an earlier candidate, solution, patch or session.

Choose and revise your own representations, contracts, auxiliary invariants and proof decomposition. Keep the async host and lab interfaces recognizable. Generate implementation and proofs together, run relevant real tests and Verus, and repair based on actual diagnostics. Preserve the fixed targets, environment, original tests, licenses and independent checker. Do not use `assume`, `admit`, external/skipped consensus bodies or fabricated results. Partial conditional results are allowed but do not close their premises.

Keep one short `PROGRESS.md` with actual changes, checks, failed approach and next obstacle, including one current obligation block and the connection summary specified in `requirements/coverage.md`. Run `python3 scripts/check.py obligation` for small code/proof attempts; the controller independently checks the selected entry and its dependencies, retains failures and prioritizes the first unfinished dependency. Begin actual initialization and handler-to-history correspondence with early core behavior, before completing all features. A CLI work slice can contain several such attempts. Keep `RESULT.md` with all lab outcomes, five theorem outcomes, actual execution and snapshot/recovery coverage, trust assumptions and reproduction commands. Use listed same-run checkpoints only when abandoning a path; scoped restoration preserves failures and cumulative spending and requires rechecking. A model theorem, table or local verified count does not establish full implementation correctness. Return normally by the prompt's soft handoff deadline; the controller independently checks the stopped candidate.

Use the existing `tools.ini` toolchain and offline dependencies. Preserve credentials, unrelated files and global tools. Do not merge, push or publish. Keep every Markdown prose paragraph on one physical line.

```bash
python3 scripts/check.py foundation
python3 scripts/check.py build
python3 scripts/check.py test raft::tests::initial_election_2a --seed 1
python3 scripts/check.py obligation --timeout 120
python3 scripts/check.py feedback --timeout 300
```

# Student implementation scope — DRAFT

The source is MadRaft at `8ec4565ecd3844f54f52865f2d7b3da4044f657f`. Complete the missing work identified by its source comments and retained tests. The supplied structs and empty request types are upstream placeholders, not an approved final data representation.

| Lab                 | Required work                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Raft 2A             | Leader election, randomized timeouts, term handling, voting and heartbeat behavior.                                                                                                              |
| Raft 2B             | Log replication, conflict repair, concurrent proposals, agreement and commit/application authorization.                                                                                          |
| Raft 2C             | Persist and restore consensus state through crashes and partitions; preserve durable voting and log decisions.                                                                                   |
| Raft 2D             | Snapshot creation, installation, compacted-log boundaries and recovery; retain all snapshot fault tests.                                                                                         |
| KV 3A/3B            | Complete server state, client routing/retries and replicated operations, then snapshot/recovery and size constraints. Derive request deduplication and retry behavior from the lab expectations. |
| Shard controller 4A | Complete replicated shard configuration operations and preserve the supplied `Config` structure.                                                                                               |
| Sharded KV 4B       | Complete clients, server state, configuration changes, shard transfer, retries, snapshots and recovery.                                                                                          |

A group has a fixed server set for its lifetime. The shard controller changes ownership of shards among groups; the upstream lab does not ask you to implement joint-consensus membership changes inside an individual Raft group. Give the controller group and each data group distinct stable identities, including across restart. Group identity and Raft term/index must not be conflated with a shard configuration number. Retiring a group does not erase its observable history.

Complete all listed labs and retained tests. Formal targets and executable correspondence requirements are in [safety.md](safety.md); environment assumptions and trust boundaries are in [environment.md](environment.md).
# Safety targets and executable correspondence — DRAFT

Use the supplied Verus definitions in [targets.rs](targets.rs). [target_checks.rs](target_checks.rs) checks examples of those definitions; [final.rs](final.rs) independently calls the implementation proofs you generate. 

| Target               | Required meaning                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Election Safety      | Across the entire history, a group elects at most one distinct leader per term.                                                                     |
| Leader Append-Only   | While a node remains leader in the same term, its logical log only extends. Physical compaction preserves the represented prefix.                   |
| Log Matching         | Within a group, entries with equal index and term imply equal prefixes through that index, including command contents, even across different times. |
| Leader Completeness  | A prefix committed in term `t` appears at its original indices in every higher-term elected leader's log in that group.                           |
| State Machine Safety | All applications at a given group and index agree on the entry, including applications before crashes and those represented by installed snapshots. |

Implement and prove at most one durable vote per term, up-to-date candidate logs, conflicting-log rejection/truncation, majority agreement and the current-term restriction for advancing leader commitment, ordered application, and faithful snapshot boundaries. These are protocol obligations, not trusted environment premises.

Generate code and proofs together. Provide `madraft/proof/implementation.rs` with the interfaces consumed by [final.rs](final.rs), using `crate::targets` and the adapters in [coverage.md](coverage.md) and importing the executable functions tested from `madraft/src/`. Describe all finite execution prefixes from actual initialization under [environment.md](environment.md). Prove initialization, transition preservation, executable correspondence and host-call preconditions; do not assume the desired safety properties or an unproved invariant.

Cover every role change, actual commit-cursor advancement, application, snapshot operation and crash/restart path, including effects in async wrappers. Preserve group and node identities, terms, original indices, exact command bytes and pre-crash history. Logical logs include their justified compacted prefixes. Do not filter execution down to passing traces or prove a disconnected model.

Prove that resident, created, installed, persisted, restored and applied snapshots faithfully represent an earlier committed prefix: boundary index and term agree, and the actual decoder yields the application state obtained by executing that prefix. Connect this claim to the real service and storage paths, retained suffix boundaries and committed/applied-prefix contract. A snapshot need not preserve a reversible command history.

Run `python3 scripts/check.py safety` for formal safety and correspondence feedback, and `final` for complete test and proof acceptance; `top NAME` checks one proof unit for feedback. Definition checks and local lemmas do not establish implementation safety. Keep incomplete properties OPEN, and report gaps in executable coverage and the trust boundary for review.
# Environment, limits and trust boundary — DRAFT

The safety model is non-Byzantine: processes execute the delivered code, peers do not forge messages or identities, serialization preserves values, and network faults may delay, reorder, duplicate or lose genuine messages and partition nodes. A reply can arrive after its initiating term or RPC is obsolete. A node can crash between host operations, losing volatile state and outstanding tasks, and restart from its retained storage. Safety must not depend on eventual delivery, a timeout bound or a majority being available. Prove the implementation's protocol invariants rather than assuming them as environmental facts.

Genuine messages are actual code emissions, including erroneous ones. The fixed proof support records prior sends without assuming their Raft correctness. A host storage completion must correspond to the actual submitted operation and result; persistence-before-reply ordering is a program obligation, not a filter that removes actual early sends.

Raft group membership is fixed and finite for each group. The group identity and member set are trusted deployment inputs, consistent across nodes and restart; a retired identity is not reused for a different group's history. Shard assignment changes are application commands, not changes to the members of a consensus group. Invalid peer IDs, malformed external inputs and finite resource exhaustion need an explicit safe rejection/failure path at the real boundary, not an unchecked helper precondition.

Host networking, the MadSim scheduler/randomness, filesystem calls, mutex/task mechanics, channel delivery, Rust memory safety, `serde`/`bincode` value encoding and the Verus/vstd/Rust/SMT implementation are trusted components under their disclosed contracts. The host may transmit, store and expose outputs chosen by verified code. Voting, log selection, commitment, application authorization, snapshot decisions and recovery interpretation may not migrate into trusted host code. List exact host functions used by the final implementation and prove the verified side meets their preconditions. No unsafe or newly trusted consensus body may close a proof gap.

The selected MadSim filesystem is an in-memory simulator. At the pinned revision, `FsSim::power_fail` is a TODO and `File::sync_all` is a no-op; completed writes already survive node kill/restart. Creating a file truncates it, and operations on different files are not one atomic transaction. The supplied MadRaft `persist` skeleton writes `state` and `snapshot` separately. A crash between create/write or between those files must not be silently excluded. Tests on this simulator do not establish real-disk crash consistency, torn-write behavior or power-loss durability. The generator must disclose the model it proves and implement a coherent storage/snapshot protocol for it. Stronger disk guarantees require explicit host contracts and separate evidence; do not claim that a simulated `sync_all` has proved them.

The starting point has no reviewed full persistent-image encoding or serialization refinement. Whether to use a single consistent state/snapshot image, recoverable generations or another scheme is the generator's design choice within the existing API and size tests. Do not assume atomic multi-file replacement to validate a chosen representation. Corrupt media and Byzantine storage are outside this initial model; ordinary crashes and incomplete operations are inside it. Failure handling must not turn an unknown durable vote into permission to vote again in the same term.

Executable counters use finite Rust types; mathematical `nat` in the targets is only an abstraction. Prove checked increment/conversion and index bounds or stop safely at exhaustion without emitting unauthorized outputs. Do not assume that terms never overflow. Bounded memory may return an error or halt a node without violating safety; allocation success or unlimited resources cannot be silently used to claim liveness. A proof over an arbitrary fixed finite membership is distinct from testing a few small clusters.

Conditional liveness is OPEN and later. It needs separate eventual leader/timing/communication fairness, scheduling and resource assumptions plus progress proofs. Passing a finite deterministic test, having an election timer or proving the five safety targets establishes none of those temporal conclusions.
# Execution correspondence and coverage — DRAFT

The five predicates in `targets.rs` retain their meanings. `final.rs` consumes the generated implementation, proves each model goal and composes them with candidate-defined runtime-relation initialization and step correspondence. Missing correspondence remains OPEN even when all five model lemmas pass. No Raft invariant or implementation is supplied.

`support.rs` provides proof adapters, not a required runtime architecture. `Envelope<M>` records group, sender, recipient and the exact payload. A `Delivery<M>` names an earlier send by its ghost sequence index. `exchange` only checks provenance and appends actual outputs: delivery may repeat, reorder or stop forever, and crash steps cannot erase prior sends. This does not require IDs in wire messages. A faulty program's actual emissions remain eligible for delivery; no vote, log or durability correctness is a network premise. Linearize multiple deliveries or host operations into justified smaller steps when needed.

For the fixed caller, export candidate types `State`, `RuntimeState`, `Input`, `Output`, `Message` and specifications `initial`, `step`, `runtime_initial`, `runtime_step`, `receive`, `emit`, `view`, `runtime_invariant`. These are adapters chosen by the generator, not prescribed MadRaft structs. `receive(input)` exposes the delivered envelope when there is one; `emit(output)` exposes all actual sends. The fixed `Execution` and `RuntimeExecution` histories contain state boundaries, actual inputs, actual outputs and cumulative sends. `execution` and `runtime_execution` use the fixed provenance rule, initially empty sends and the candidate's corresponding initialization/step relations. `abstract_execution` projects states through `view`, preserving every input, output and send record.

`prove_runtime_initial(s)` must establish the candidate's invariant at empty send history and model initialization for every executable initial state. `prove_runtime_step(s,i,t,o,a,b)` must establish invariant preservation and the projected model step from executable step, prior invariant and `exchange(a,receive(i),emit(o),b)`. `final.rs` checks these explicit conclusions and invokes the verified generic `simulate` theorem. `support::invariant_at` is also available for any candidate invariant: initialization and every admitted step must establish it. The parameters are proof obligations, not assumed Raft facts. See the small executable counter in `support_example.rs`, verified by `python3 scripts/check.py foundation`; it is a usage example, not protocol code.

Generate the concrete connection to actual constructors, handler segments, sends and host completions in the same source imported by Rust tests and Verus. Show that every allowed executable path satisfies `runtime_initial` or `runtime_step`, that `receive` and `emit` preserve exact messages and identities, and that `view` retains the state needed for observations. This semantic adequacy is not automatically decided by defining an adapter or importing a source file. The coverage direction is all allowed actual executions into the checked history relation. Empty/false relations or omitting difficult paths are not permitted. Record exact function names, contracts and their callers in `PROGRESS.md` and the final `RESULT.md`; these notes remain review evidence, not machine proof.

Provide `observe(Execution)`, the five `prove_PROPERTY(Execution)` lemmas, `applications()` and `prove_observation_and_snapshots(Execution)` for the fixed callers. The latter establishes `targets::shape` and `targets::snapshot_fidelity`. `execution_witness()` returns a `RuntimeExecution` satisfying `runtime_execution`, observation shape and at least one non-Silent event after projection. This necessary witness is neither exhaustive coverage nor liveness. The aggregate caller concludes all five predicates and snapshot fidelity for every admitted candidate runtime history; it cannot combine partial passes from different candidate definitions.

Storage completion must identify a real submitted operation and its actual result. Do not inject success as an unconstrained input, assume multi-file atomicity, or rule out a reply that faulty code actually sends before persistence. Prove the required ordering in the program. RPC replies identify actual requests and handling peers; old genuine replies remain deliverable. Elections, commit-cursor changes, applications, snapshots and recovery observations must reflect actual behavior, with pre-crash history retained. Compacted logical prefixes need a real origin; decoding snapshot bytes into application state remains a candidate obligation under `environment.md`.

For partial feedback, `top NAME` uses `madraft/proof/NAME.rs` when provided, otherwise `implementation.rs`. Export only the interfaces consumed by that caller and share actual dependencies through `crate::support` and `crate::targets`; the fixed caller exports `crate::Execution` and `crate::execution`, plus runtime aliases for execution/witness checks. Separate unrelated unfinished theorem bodies into other files. Every imported body is verified with `--no-cheating`; no function filtering is used. `safety` verifies formal composition without Cargo tests. `final` includes all test families, all configured seeds, foundation/definition checks, all top-level goals and the aggregate on one stopped candidate.

Source-link scans and literal vacuity checks detect a few obvious mistakes, not arbitrary semantic equivalence. Review runtime path coverage, real caller preconditions, asynchronous coordination, message extraction, observation completeness, snapshot decoders and the declared host TCB even after a machine pass. Finite-history induction proves no conditional liveness result.

The report separates formula verification, nominated actual-connection proof units, and complete implementation acceptance. `execution_link` checks the runtime-relation to model-relation projection, including preservation of inputs/outputs/sends. It does not alone prove that actual code obeys the runtime relation. A PASS remains a mathematical PASS even when actual callers, outputs or recovery are not covered. Even MACHINE_CHECKS_PASSED leaves semantic review NOT_PERFORMED and implementation acceptance NOT_ESTABLISHED; there is no interactive approval checkpoint in generation.

Maintain exactly one short connection table in PROGRESS.md between the markers below. Each row names one candidate proof unit and comma-separated actual function references in `madraft/src/file.rs::function` form. Extend the nominated unit or split auxiliary files as needed; these five review areas are not a fixed implementation architecture or task sequence. Preserve open premises in the last column. The checker independently runs the nominated unit even when an outer reference is absent or not imported. It retains the unit result and separately lists imported-reference hints and unconnected paths; none of these scans is proof of caller semantics. A passing unit still requires review of actual call coverage; declarations alone cannot establish implementation-level acceptance. Do not duplicate this table in JSON.

```markdown
<!-- connections -->
| Behavior | Actual functions | Proof entry | Open premises / next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| initialization | madraft/src/your_file.rs::constructor | madraft/proof/your_initialization.rs | Actual constructor and callee preconditions remain open. |
| transitions | madraft/src/your_file.rs::handler | madraft/proof/your_callers.rs | Input authorization and real caller composition remain open. |
| outputs | madraft/src/your_file.rs::release | madraft/proof/your_outputs.rs | Send/storage/application output correspondence remains open. |
| recovery | madraft/src/your_file.rs::restore | madraft/proof/your_recovery.rs | Re-establish subsequent preconditions from durable state and history. |
| snapshots | madraft/src/your_file.rs::install | madraft/proof/your_snapshots.rs | Creation, installation, decoding and recovery remain open. |
<!-- /connections -->
```

Names in this example are placeholders, not supplied functions or required filenames. Cover all real paths within each area, including state changes made by async coordination. An internal action cannot freely insert a log entry or assume a quorum: its actual input and caller context must justify it. The common support examples demonstrate real-function/model and recovery/caller obligations without any Raft implementation or invariant. See `restore_then_update`: ghost history need not be persisted, but recovery must prove its relation before calling a verified operation.

Select one current obligation in the following flat block in PROGRESS.md. Replace every example value with your own bounded assignment. `goal` names a fixed top-level target; `parent` is its concrete upper use or an intermediate caller, not just a sentence claiming usefulness. `kind` is local, caller, initialization, step or composition. Comma-separated `dependencies` are ordered prerequisite proof units; keep each unit small and complete. `tests` contains existing Rust test filters, never shell commands. Blank optional fields are allowed. All candidate proof paths stay under madraft/src or madraft/proof. This block is a plan, not evidence, and creates no fixed Raft architecture.

Run `python3 scripts/check.py obligation --timeout 120` to check this increment, including its ordered dependencies, entry, parent and selected tests. The controller rechecks the stopped candidate and independently replays up to three saved obligation microchecks per handoff under the cumulative budget; candidate-authored logs alone never establish progress. `runs/attempts.jsonl` is the controller's append-only evidence view. Each checked version retains source, commands and diagnostics. Changing a statement invalidates current evidence; changing an id or overlapping entry does not reset its recorded attempts. Review the first unfinished dependency before choosing the next increment. After two substantive handoffs with buildable protocol changes/local results but no checked initialization or step nomination, continuation prioritizes establishing that connection. This scheduling heuristic is not semantic coverage certification.

Reports distinguish interface preparation, a checked local unit and a checked parent unit with unreviewed premises. An imported parent is only a use-site hint: inspect that it actually invokes the result and discharges the intended premises. Explicit `requires` remain conditional until actual initialization and preserved steps establish them. Do not put unproved protocol facts into execution or environment assumptions. The aggregate still verifies every fixed property, execution, observation and snapshot obligation on the same candidate with all retained tests/seeds.

When an approach is abandoned, optionally add `rollback = cp-N` and `restore = src/your_core.rs, proof/your_initialization.rs` inside the same block, using only a checkpoint listed by this run's controller. Restoration includes the checkpoint's and current obligation's named code and transitive proof dependencies; explicitly name any additional affected candidate source/proof files. Protected requirements/tests and outside paths cannot be restored. The controller preserves the failed snapshot/diff and diagnostics, restores that scope, removes newly added files in the scope and rechecks affected work. Unrelated files remain. If representation changes affect more callers, include them and report the impact. Budget, session, failures and redesign counts never roll back. Checkpoints labeled BUILDABLE or LOCAL_UNIT_CHECKED are not globally verified programs.

Three actual failed proof attempts without a newly checked related unit trigger reconsideration of this obligation. Missing entries, compilation failures, unavailable tools and timeouts have separate repair routes and do not count as mathematical dead ends. The default allows two redesigns per obligation and six in the run; reaching a limit requires a different necessary dependency or an honest stop. Renaming an obligation sharing its entries/functions retains that history; arbitrary semantic identity is still a review responsibility. Conditional liveness remains OPEN.
